```{r setup, include = FALSE}
live <- identical(Sys.getenv("ICONIFYR_LIVE_VIGNETTES"), "true")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = live)
library(iconifyr)
```

Every icon set on Iconify has its own license. Using an icon means following
that license. This page shows how to look it up. It is not legal advice.

## Look up a license

```{r license}
lic <- iconify_license("fa6-solid")
lic
```

`iconify_license()` accepts a set prefix or a full icon id. When the license
requires attribution (Creative Commons Attribution licenses such as CC BY 4.0,
and ODbL), it also prints a message. Silence it with `quiet = TRUE`.

The result is a list, so you can build a credit line from it:

```{r credit}
sprintf("Icons: %s by %s (%s), %s", lic$set, lic$author, lic$url, lic$license)
```

## Audit all sets

`iconify_sets()` has the license of every set, so you can filter before you
pick one:

```{r audit}
sets <- iconify_sets()
table(sets$license_spdx, useNA = "ifany")[1:8]
head(sets[grepl("^(MIT|Apache)", sets$license_spdx), c("prefix", "name", "license_spdx")])
```

## What the attribution flag covers

- `attribution_required` is `TRUE` for SPDX ids starting with `CC-BY` (this
  includes CC-BY-SA and CC-BY-NC) and for `ODbL`.
- MIT, Apache-2.0 and BSD sets don't require visible credit, but they require
  you to keep the license notice when you redistribute the icons.
- Sets with no license data return `NA`. Check the set's source.
- Non-commercial and share-alike licenses carry extra conditions beyond
  attribution. Read the license URL.
